purpose: Define the movement intent, hard constraints, measurable targets, coaching cues, and compensation signals that a synthesized bodyweight squat must satisfy before it can be treated as a valid squat reference.

authorityBoundary.notes: Compensation signals are coaching/assessment observations, not diagnoses. Geometry targets require avatar- or MoveNet-specific calibration.

stance.cue: Stand with both feet planted at a comfortable approximately shoulder-width stance.
stance.measurement: stance width normalized to avatar/user shoulder width

feet.cue: Keep the whole foot planted through the squat.

insideKneeAngleDegrees.notes: Measure from the actual avatar/user hip-knee-ankle geometry; do not infer from authored bone rotation constants alone.

referenceSideGeometry.notes: These are generator constraints for this canonical reference squat, not universal human squat scoring rules. The runtime should measure actual world/side-projected joint markers before accepting a generated reference.

kneeTracking.sideViewRule: for the canonical generated reference squat, forward knee travel is constrained while the pelvis must travel posteriorly and whole-foot contact remains stable
kneeTracking.notes: The generator uses a stricter toe-line envelope for this reference animation because the selected coaching style is sit-back dominant. Do not reuse this as a universal human movement-screen failure rule without exercise/style-specific calibration.

coachCues: Sit the hips down and back like sitting into a chair.
Keep the knees tracking with the feet and inside the configured reference toe-line envelope.
Stay balanced through the whole foot.
Stand back up by extending the hips and knees together.

compensationSignals.meaning: loss of whole-foot contact or insufficient coordinated ankle/hip strategy
knee moves inward relative to foot/hip line
knee moves materially outward relative to foot/hip line
foot rotates outward materially during the movement
arch/foot position visibly collapses during the movement
pelvis/body shifts materially toward one side
torso lean dominates instead of coordinated hip-knee-ankle squat mechanics
bottom knee-angle/depth target is not reached
pelvis drops without enough backward travel for the selected sit-back reference style
generated reference knee travels farther forward than the configured toe-line envelope
